assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine formation from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine, general operation. It is among the most heavily used bond constructions in pharmaceutical and agrochemical process chemistry and in materials work, and the ligand-design logic (bulky biaryl phosphines, hindered alkylphosphines) enabled a whole later generation of catalysts. Squarely molecule-making with conceptual simplicity and enormous adoption.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, practical catalyst systems independently and in parallel; Kosugi and Migita's earlier tin-amide work is the precursor, and Kosugi is credited here, but the generality and mechanism came from the other two. A two-person prize is clean. Migita is not on the credited list, which I flag but cannot fix.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of independent confirmation and thousands of later syntheses and industrial processes. Recognition is, if anything, overdue; the 2010 cross-coupling prize left this area out.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would regard this as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling recognition.
I have not independently verified the precise priority details of the 1994-1995 Kosugi, Buchwald and Hartwig papers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis changed what bond constructions are practical: single-electron pathways with mild light-driven catalysts, radical generation from abundant functional groups, and the dual-catalysis concept merging photoredox with organo-, nickel and other catalysis. It has been absorbed into medicinal chemistry and late-stage functionalization, and is clearly a new way of making bonds.
assessment.attribution: Yoon (2008), Stephenson (2009) and MacMillan (2008) published the founding synthetic demonstrations in a near-simultaneous burst; Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi are also strong. A three-person selection is defensible but excludes others of real merit, so allocation is contested. MacMillan has already received the 2021 prize for organocatalysis, which may weigh against him.
assessment.maturity: Over 15 years of broad independent adoption in industry and academia; maturity is high, though the field is still evolving rapidly and the early Ru/Ir bipyridyl photophysics predates the synthetic work.
uncertainties: Whether a prior laureate should be included given the 2021 prize.
Credit relative to earlier photochemistry (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier) and the mechanistic work on chain versus catalytic pathways.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists treat ubiquitous C-H bonds as functional handles, shortening syntheses and enabling late-stage diversification. The directing-group and ligand-controlled Pd chemistry (Yu, Sanford) and Ir-catalyzed borylation (Hartwig, Smith) are real strategy-level advances in step economy, the efficiency theme I care about.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over several mechanistically distinct strands: directed Pd(II) catalysis, ligand-accelerated meta/enantioselective C-H activation, and undirected borylation. Yu, Sanford and Hartwig are the most defensible trio, but this is a compound field whose parts may need different treatment, and it overlaps in name with my rank-1 choice.
assessment.maturity: Roughly two decades of development with growing but still uneven adoption in industrial route design; not yet as routine as cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Industrial uptake is real but narrower than for cross-coupling.
Choice of which strand to honour is unresolved.
Possible overlap with Hartwig on the C-N coupling candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes showed that these long-proposed reactive species could be bottled, and NHCs then became ubiquitous ligands (including in Grubbs-type metathesis catalysts) and organocatalysts. The (alkyl)(amino)carbene work widened the reactivity range. Conceptually clean, with lasting effect on organometallic and main-group synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's 1988 phosphinocarbene and Arduengo's 1991 crystalline imidazol-2-ylidene are the decisive isolation steps. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are important for application, but the discovery credit sits with the first two. Two names is a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: More than 30 years of confirmation and extremely widespread use as ligands and catalysts; fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views NHC ligands in metathesis as already recognised via the 2005 prize.
Bertrand's 1988 compound's carbene character was debated, which affects priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs gave chemists direct control over protein composition in living cells. It opened a route from organic chemistry to protein function, with wide use in bioorthogonal labelling, photocrosslinking and protein engineering. Chemically novel in design, though the venue is biological.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the amber-suppression and evolved orthogonal pair approach in E. coli and then in other hosts; Chin extended it to eukaryotes and multi-site, quadruplet and ribosome-orthogonal systems. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama are also contributors, so a two-person pick leaves out credible names.
assessment.maturity: Over 20 years of broad independent use; established, with continuing extensions.
uncertainties: The 'what was new chemically' question is partly answered by evolved synthetases, which is closer to biology.
Attribution among Schultz, Chin, Wang and Mehl is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable, automated solid-phase DNA synthesis possible and underpins PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and oligonucleotide therapeutics. It is a case of a conceptually simple synthetic method becoming infrastructure for all of molecular biology, and its chemistry is squarely mine.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method (with Beaucage in the key 1981 deprotection and activation step, who is not credited here). The supplied list includes Hood, whose contribution was instrument automation, so a Caruthers-only proposal is the most defensible among the supplied names, but leaves a partner question open.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use; fully mature and arguably late.
uncertainties: Beaucage's role is not represented in the credited names.
Hood's automation role may be considered engineering rather than chemistry.
The method is old, so the question is why it was not already recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation via PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality built on chemically designed heterobifunctional molecules, now in many clinical trials. Medicinal-chemistry design rules are still being worked out, but the conceptual change is large.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies created the first PROTAC concept; Ciulli did structural and VHL-ligand design work. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito) is a distinct, comparably important discovery, so a compound candidate whose parts could need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still ongoing; timeliness is plausible but there is some prematurity risk.
uncertainties: Clinical efficacy at scale is not yet established as a prize-grade outcome.
Allocation between PROTAC and molecular-glue lines is unresolved.
Primary framing is medicinal chemistry rather than synthesis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation and expressed protein ligation made total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine, with chemoselective peptide-bond formation in water. It is a methodology advance with lasting effect on protein chemistry and chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir, Kent (and Dawson with Kent) published the foundational 1994 NCL work, and Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are significant for later developments, which complicates a trio.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use; mature, but practical impact has been more limited than the genuinely general synthetic methods ranked above.
uncertainties: Breadth of adoption outside specialist laboratories is less clear to me.
Whether the committee would see the work as peptide chemistry too specialised.
